analysis.title: Americas Pipelines and MLPs: Remain Constructive on Natural Gas Pipelines After Recent Volatility; Focus on Buy-Rated WMB and TRP; DTM Up to Neutral
key_insights: GS stays constructive on natural gas pipelines despite the debate over data center power growth, citing 3Q26 earnings updates and possible permitting reform. The coverage group (AM, DTM, ENB, ET, KMI, TRP, WMB) is down 5% over six months versus AMZ down 1%.

GS gives four reasons the group is well positioned: lower-beta exposure to gas demand growth, high contracting with little pre-FID EBITDA in near-to-medium-term estimates, 3Q26 updates showing more utility and hyperscaler willingness to support gas projects, and recent permit reform progress in Washington.

WMB is the top idea for the theme. GS's ~12% EBITDA CAGR for 2025-30 is described as compelling but reflecting only modest new project wins, with the post-FID CAGR already at ~11%. GS expects power project FIDs before year-end.
TRP (Buy) is highlighted after a strong 3Q26 update and a new Canada power opportunity. KMI (Buy) is favored ahead of project announcements, with modestly increased risk.
DTM is upgraded to Neutral from Sell after underperformance, a reset in 2030 EBITDA expectations, and a likely larger backlog update at 4Q26.

GS keeps its data center estimate unchanged: ~10-11 bcf/d of incremental US gas demand by 2030, based on ~108 GW of US data center power demand by 2030 (~69 GW of growth 2025-2030). Gas is assumed to fuel ~60% of the ~47 GW on-grid growth and 100% of the ~22 GW behind-the-meter growth. GS calls this the low end of industry forecasts of 10-15+ bcf/d.

Gas transmission CAGRs of 5-10% for 2026-2032 are described as highly compelling for a sector normally at low single-digit growth. GS sees a mix shift toward demand-pull (utility power, LNG feedgas) and away from supply-push.

Sanctioned backlogs equal ~14-15% of 2026 EV across coverage. Build multiples are ~6x for many projects against run-rate valuations of ~12x. Almost all 2026-28 incremental EBITDA growth for the group is already sanctioned.

The Senate voted to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) permitting bill, and President Trump endorsed it. GS lists broad NEPA exemptions for existing corridors, narrower state authority under the Clean Water Act, and faster permitting deadlines. GS takes no view on final passage and sees project announcements accelerating as soon as 2H27 if it passes.

Looser permitting could lower barriers to entry for new pipeline developers and erode the regional franchises of existing pipelines over time. GS still expects near- to medium-term effects to be positive for coverage.

Price targets embed 12.5-15x 2027E EBITDA for gas-weighted names. On 2030E, implied EV/EBITDA compresses to 8.0-13.0x, and the average across gas coverage compresses about two turns from 2027E to 2030E.
WMB has the most multiple compression: the 15x 2027E target multiple falls to 11.4x by 2030 on ~41% EBITDA growth 2027-2030E. DTM and AM compression depends more on pre-FID projects.
WMB price target is $82, down from $84, on 15x 2027E EBITDA of $9,777m. Higher non-controlling interests drive the cut. NESE in-service timing is left at 2Q28 against management guidance of 4Q27.

TRP price target is C$102 / US$73 (from C$101 / US$71) on 14.75x 2027E EBITDA of C$12,393m. TRP has ~89% of 2032E EBITDA in gas transmission, a sanctioned US$1.8b Crossroads project (GS had expected US$1.4b), and ~C$25b of pre-FID gas and ~C$15b of pre-FID power opportunities, with the power projects excluded from estimates.

KMI price target is $36 (unchanged) on 12.5x 2027E EBITDA. The Southeast Connector could be upsized to ~3.5 bcf/d from 2.6 bcf/d after bids awarded on 10/23/2026, and the Permian Link project is anchored by a single hyperscaler customer. Risks include 2027 guidance next month, possible RNG M&A, and Georgia policy risk tied to the Southern Company JV.

DTM price target rises to $127 from $121, with the multiple raised to 13.5x from 13x on 2027E EBITDA. Consensus 2030 EBITDA for DTM is down 5% in six months, implying an ~8.5% CAGR for 2025-2030 against GS at ~9%. The stock fell 16% over six months against a 3% decline for gas-weighted peers.

GS expects DTM to raise its five-year organic backlog from ~$3.4b to roughly $4.3-4.8b at 4Q26 earnings, about a 35% increase at the midpoint. If 70% of that is sanctioned within 12 months, sanctioned backlog could reach ~19-21% of EV against ~15% now.

ET stays Neutral with a $22 target (unchanged) on 8.75x. Gas transmission has the highest EBITDA CAGR in coverage (10%, 2026-2032E) but is only ~27% of the business. Recontracting headwinds in NGL and crude leave ET with the lowest total EBITDA CAGR (2%). ET has the lowest 2030E implied multiple (8.0x) and the least multiple compression (0.8x).

AM stays Neutral and its target falls to $23 from $24 as the multiple drops to 10.5x from 11x, reflecting higher risk to Antero Resources' growth amid a softer gas backdrop. Gas transmission is only ~8% of 2032E EBITDA.

ENB stays Neutral with targets of C$71 / US$50 (from C$70 / US$49) on 13x 2027E EBITDA. Gas pipelines are ~30% of 2032E EBITDA, leverage is 5.1x at 3Q26 against a target range below that, and the pending Tallgrass (US$2.55b) and Laramie (US$485m) deals are excluded from estimates. GS looks to the December guidance update.

Geographic risks to watch: Ohio and Texas for WMB behind-the-meter projects, Georgia for KMI after the PSC turned Democrat-controlled, the Midwest for TRP and DTM, and New Mexico for ET's Desert Southwest project. GS flags Louisiana as increasingly positive and Venture Global as a relative beneficiary, and says Texas behind-the-meter projects could benefit Kodiak Gas, LandBridge and WaterBridge.

sector_views.rationale: Growth is anchored by take-or-pay contracts and demand-pull opportunities, 5-10% transmission CAGRs, and sanctioned backlogs of ~14-15% of EV, with permitting reform as a possible catalyst.

earnings_insights: WMB: GS estimates ~12% EBITDA CAGR 2025-30, with ~11% already supported by post-FID projects. 2027E EBITDA is $9,777m (GS estimate) and new estimates are within 1% of prior.

TRP: 3Q26 update (reported) was described as strong, with the Crossroads project sanctioned at US$1.8b. GS 2027E EBITDA is C$12,393m against company guidance of C$12.3-12.5b. GS 2031E EBITDA of C$15.51b is below TRP's implied 2031 guidance of C$15.92b. TRP guided to a 5-7% EBITDA CAGR for 2026-31.
KMI: 3Q26 results showed power-driven demand proof points. GS 2027E EBITDA is $9,084m, about 2% below consensus on average over 2027-2030. KMI gives 2027 guidance next month.

DTM: GS 2027E EBITDA is $1,285m (GS estimate). Consensus 2030 EBITDA is down 5% in six months. The next catalyst is 4Q26 earnings with a backlog update, and GS estimates an ~8.7% EBITDA CAGR for 2025-2032.

ET: GS 2026E EBITDA of $19.59b (GS estimate) is up 2% from prior and compares with consensus of $19.57b. GS 2027E is $18,999m and sits ~3% below consensus on average over 2027-2030. 2030 consensus is up ~6% in six months.
AM: GS EBITDA estimates are unchanged from the recent recap note. GS is in line with consensus this year and next and above consensus from 2028 on. 2027E EBITDA is $1,315m (GS estimate).
ENB: GS 2026E EBITDA of C$20.52b (GS estimate) is in line with the midpoint of the C$20.2-20.8b guidance range. Leverage was 5.1x at 3Q26. The December guidance update is the next catalyst.
Coverage-wide: 3Q26 earnings updates are described as constructive, showing more willingness from utilities and hyperscalers to support gas projects.

trade_ideas.description: Long WMB (Buy, $82 target), GS's top idea for the natural gas pipeline theme
trade_ideas.rationale: WMB has industry-leading EBITDA growth and the most multiple compression through 2030, and GS expects 1-2 power project announcements to lift the stock.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower-than-expected gas recovery, softer execution on gas and power projects, higher regulatory hurdles, and high-multiple bolt-on M&A.

trade_ideas.rationale: TRP has the most direct gas transmission exposure, a strong 3Q26 update and a new Canada power opportunity.
trade_ideas.risk: Softer execution on gas and power projects, regulatory hurdles, slower deleveraging, and higher capex.

trade_ideas.description: Long KMI (Buy, $36 target) into upcoming project announcements
trade_ideas.rationale: Project announcements should improve the market's view of KMI's ability to execute commercially.
trade_ideas.risk: 2027 guidance, possible RNG M&A, and Georgia policy and rate-case exposure.

risk_factors: Risks to pre-FID backlog execution after the recent elections.
Permitting timelines for new greenfield projects could lengthen, and state-level approvals for data center projects are uncertain.
Slower LNG feedgas demand growth, expected by the early 2030s, and renewables penetration reducing system utilization.
Looser permitting could erode the regional pipeline franchises over time by lowering barriers to entry.
ENB leverage of 5.1x is above target, and the pending Tallgrass and Laramie acquisitions add a leverage question.
NGL and crude recontracting headwinds at ET.
KMI exposure to Georgia regulation, 2027 guidance and possible RNG M&A.
Execution on DTM's pre-FID projects and the risk of a smaller-than-expected backlog update.
vol_and_positioning: DTM has fallen 16% over six months against a 3% decline for gas-weighted midstream peers, and is flat YTD against peers up 13%.
The coverage group is down 5% over six months against AMZ down 1%.
DTM now trades closer to WMB and KMI after a prior ~1.5-2x premium, and DTM shares have risen 124% since being added to the Americas Sell list on October 5, 2023, against 79% for the S&P 500.
geopolitical: Post-election uncertainty over on-grid data center approvals and state-level permitting, including Georgia's PSC turning Democrat-controlled.
The Senate voted to advance the BAAJA permitting reform bill, and President Trump publicly endorsed it.
GS flags risk that draconian post-election permitting scenarios could slow new project announcements.

tension_points.theme: gas pipeline permitting and data center demand
tension_points.bull_case: Permitting reform (BAAJA) could lower execution risk, capex costs and in-service times. A large share of growth is already sanctioned and contracted, and demand-pull drivers support 5-10% transmission CAGRs.
tension_points.bear_case: Post-election regulatory uncertainty could lengthen permitting for new greenfield projects and slow new project announcements. Looser permitting could also erode existing pipeline franchises over time, and there is debate over the data center power outlook.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure of the permitting bill to pass the Senate and House, or draconian post-election permitting outcomes that slow new project announcements.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth expectations have reset, negative revisions look worked through, and the backlog could rise to $4.3-4.8b at 4Q26.
tension_points.bear_case: A large share of growth depends on pre-FID projects such as Vector 2030, MIST Phase 2+ and Millennium, and conversion to FID remains an execution hurdle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 4Q26 backlog update below the expected $4.3-4.8b, or slower or smaller conversion of pre-FID projects to FID.

theme_stances.key_argument: Contracted, demand-pull growth and sanctioned backlogs support a compelling outlook for gas pipelines despite the data center debate.
theme_stances.evidence: We remain constructive on the natural gas pipeline subsector

theme_stances.key_argument: The market is under-appreciating progress on permitting reform and its effect on execution risk, capex and in-service dates.
theme_stances.evidence: the market is under-appreciating the progress that has been made

theme_stances.key_argument: Mostly contracted growth should compress implied multiples through 2030, with WMB showing the most compression.
theme_stances.evidence: implied multiple compression through 2030 as the more relevant valuation framework
